symptom: swelling of the feet in an older person, often from poor circulation or heart trouble
citation: Chapter 22: Health and Sicknesses of Older People
summary: Swelling of the feet can be caused by many diseases, but in older people it is often caused by poor circulation or heart trouble. Whatever the cause, the book states that keeping the feet up is the best treatment, walking helps too, but not spending much time standing or sitting with the feet down, and keeping the feet up whenever possible. This entry is kept separate from the pregnancy foot-swelling entry and from the heart-trouble entry because Chapter 22 presents older-person foot swelling as its own presentation with its own simple management, while also pointing to heart trouble as a possible underlying cause.
when_to_seek_care: not stated in the book

symptom: swelling of the feet in pregnancy, and swelling of hands and face
citation: Chapter 19: Information for Mothers and Midwives
summary: Swelling of the feet in pregnancy is helped by resting at different times during the day with the feet up, eating less salt and avoiding salty foods, and the book mentions tea made from maize silk as possibly helping. Swelling of the feet usually comes from the pressure of the child in the womb during the last months and is worse in women who are anemic or malnourished, so eating plenty of nutritious food is advised. The distinction the book draws is important: ordinary foot swelling in late pregnancy is listed as a minor problem, while very swollen feet together with swelling of the hands and face is a warning sign to seek medical advice and is also part of the pre-eclampsia presentation.
danger_signs: feet very swollen, with hands and face also swelling
when_to_seek_care: If the feet are very swollen and the hands and face also swell, seek medical advice.

citation: Chapter 13: Swelling of the Feet and Other Parts of the Body
danger_signs: swelling of the face or other parts of the body as well as the feet, usually a sign of serious illness
in pregnancy, high blood pressure, swollen face, a lot of protein in urine, or sudden weight gain, possibly pre-eclampsia
review_note: Swelling has many unrelated causes in this section, so this entry groups them as a presenting sign and flags the pregnancy and whole-body patterns rather than giving one diagnosis.
summary: Swelling of the feet may be caused by a number of problems, some minor and others serious, but if the face or other parts of the body are also swollen, this is usually a sign of serious illness. Women's feet sometimes swell in the last three months of pregnancy, usually not serious, but with high blood pressure, swollen face, protein in urine or sudden weight gain it may be pre-eclampsia. Old people may get swollen feet from poor circulation, heart trouble or kidney disease, and small children from anemia or malnutrition, including kwashiorkor.
symptom: swollen feet
when_to_seek_care: Seek medical help fast if a pregnant woman has swollen feet with high blood pressure, swollen face, protein in urine, or sudden weight gain.

symptom: swollen, painful, inflamed lymph nodes in the groin or anus that may burst, drain pus, scar and reopen (buboes)
citation: Chapter 18: The Urinary System and the Genitals
summary: Buboes are infected lymph nodes that are inflamed, swollen and painful, and may burst, drain pus, scar and reopen. Some sexually transmitted infections cause buboes in the lymph nodes on one or both sides of the genitals or in the anus, most often caused by a chlamydia virus, though buboes in the groin can also be a sign of chancroid. The book advises seeing a health worker for testing and treatment, gives antibiotic treatment as directed on its medicine pages with different advice for people who are pregnant or breastfeeding, and advises avoiding sex until sores are completely healed, antibiotic treatment is completed, and all partners are also treated.
when_to_seek_care: See a health worker for testing and treatment.

symptom: swollen testicle in a baby boy, on one side of the scrotum (hydrocele or hernia)
citation: Chapter 21: Health and Sicknesses of Children
summary: If a baby's scrotum, the bag holding the testicles, is swollen on one side, this is usually because it is filled with liquid, a hydrocele, or because a loop of gut has slipped into it, a hernia. Shining a light through the swelling helps tell them apart: if light shines through easily it is probably a hydrocele, while if light does not shine through and the swelling gets bigger when the baby coughs or cries, it is a hernia. Sometimes a hernia causes swelling in the groin in either a boy or a girl, distinguished from a swollen lymph node because the hernia swells when the baby cries or is held upright and disappears when lying quietly. A hydrocele usually goes away in time without treatment.
when_to_seek_care: If a hydrocele lasts more than a year, get medical advice; a hernia needs surgery.

symptom: swollen veins in the legs in pregnancy (varicose veins) and piles (hemorrhoids)
citation: Chapter 19: Information for Mothers and Midwives
summary: Swollen veins in pregnancy are common due to the weight of the baby pressing on the veins that come from the legs. The book advises putting the feet up often as high as possible, and if the veins get very big or hurt, wrapping them with an elastic bandage or using elastic stockings, taken off at night. Piles are varicose veins in the anus resulting from the weight of the baby in the womb. To relieve the pain the book advises kneeling with the buttocks in the air or sitting in a basin of cool water, and cross-refers to its varicose veins section. No danger signs are stated for these presentations in this section.
when_to_seek_care: not stated in the book

citation: Chapter 12: Tapeworm
danger_signs: cysts in the brain causing headaches, seizures, or death
summary: Tapeworms grow several meters long in the intestines, but the small flat white segments found in feces are usually about one centimeter, and occasionally a segment crawls out into underclothing. People get them from eating pork, beef or other meat or fish that is not well cooked. Intestinal tapeworms sometimes cause mild stomach aches but few other problems. The greatest danger is when cysts get into the brain, which happens when eggs pass from stools to mouth through lack of cleanliness.
symptom: tapeworm infection
when_to_seek_care: Anyone with tapeworms should get treatment as soon as possible.

symptom: tearing of the birth opening during birth
citation: Chapter 19: Information for Mothers and Midwives
summary: The birth opening must stretch a lot for the baby to come out and sometimes it tears, more likely if it is the mother's first baby. Tearing can usually be prevented with care: the mother should try to stop pushing when the baby's head is coming out to give the birth opening time to stretch, the midwife can support the stretching opening with one hand while gently keeping the head from coming too fast with the other, and warm compresses against the skin below the birth opening and massaging the stretched skin with oil may also help. If a tear does happen, someone who knows how should carefully sew it shut after the placenta comes out.
when_to_seek_care: If a tear happens, it should be sewn shut by someone who knows how, after the placenta comes out.

alternate_names: newborn who cannot suck and cries continuously
citation: Chapter 14: Tetanus (Lockjaw)
danger_signs: jaw getting stiff, then neck and other muscles getting stiff
painful convulsions of the jaw and finally the whole body, triggered by moving, touching, sudden noise or bright light
summary: Tetanus results when a germ living in animal or human feces enters through a wound, especially deep or dirty wounds, animal bites, gunshot and knife wounds, barbed wire injuries, and puncture wounds from thorns, splinters or nails, or through a newborn's umbilical cord cut without cleanliness. Signs are an infected wound, discomfort and difficulty swallowing, a stiff jaw, then stiff neck and body muscles with difficulty walking, and painful convulsions. In a newborn, first signs generally appear three to ten days after birth, with continuous crying and inability to suck.
symptom: tetanus
when_to_seek_care: Seek medical help at the first sign; if a newborn cries continuously or stops nursing, suspect tetanus and act.

symptom: thick, milky vaginal discharge with a rancid smell (bacterial vaginal infection)
citation: Chapter 18: The Urinary System and the Genitals
summary: Thick, milky discharge with a rancid smell could be an infection caused by bacteria. The book states that tests may be needed to tell this from a Trichomonas infection and cross-refers to its sections on common sexually transmitted infections and how to treat them. It gives no separate treatment for this discharge type in this section, and the general discharge advice applies: discharge with an unusual colour, bad smell, itching or pain, belly pain, pain while urinating or having sex, or fever may be caused by an infection, some of which are dangerous if not treated quickly.
when_to_seek_care: If any discharge lasts a long time or does not get better with treatment, see a health worker.
review_note: The book itself says tests may be needed to distinguish this from Trichomonas, so this entry records the presentation only and should not be used to choose treatment.

symptom: thick, rough patches of reddish or blue-grey skin covered with whitish or silver scales, especially on elbows and knees, lasting a long time or coming back (psoriasis)
citation: Chapter 15: Skin Problems
summary: Psoriasis shows as thick, rough patches of reddish or blue-grey skin covered with whitish or silver-coloured scales, most commonly on the elbows and knees and other parts shown in the chapter drawings. The condition usually lasts a long time or keeps coming back, and the book states it is not an infection and is not dangerous. Leaving the affected skin open to sunlight often helps and bathing in the ocean sometimes helps. The book advises seeking medical advice, noting that treatment must be continued for a long time.
when_to_seek_care: Seek medical advice; treatment must be continued for a long time.

citation: Chapter 2: Sicknesses that Are Often Confused
danger_signs: weight loss over an extended time, listed in Chapter 4 among signs of dangerous illness
review_note: This presentation has many unrelated possible causes in Chapter 2 and cannot be narrowed to one condition from this chapter alone; later chapters must be consulted before any specific mapping.
summary: Chapter 2 uses a child who slowly becomes thin and wasted while the belly gets more and more swollen as an example of illnesses that are hard to tell apart. Possible problems listed are malnutrition, a large number of roundworms usually together with malnutrition, advanced tuberculosis, a long-term severe urinary infection, several problems of the liver or spleen, leukemia, and HIV. The chapter stresses that medical treatment differs for each disease, so telling them apart matters, and that diseases do not always show the signs described. Skilled help or special tests are often needed for difficult cases, and the examiner should work within their limits.
symptom: thin, wasted child with swollen belly
when_to_seek_care: Get medical help, especially if the illness seems serious or the cause is not fairly sure.

symptom: toothache from a cavity (hole caused by decay)
citation: Chapter 17: The Teeth, Gums, and Mouth
summary: Painful cavities and sore gums can be prevented by good tooth care, and the book stresses avoiding sweets, brushing well every day and always immediately after eating anything sweet, and using fluoride where natural fluoride is lacking. If a tooth already has a cavity, the book advises avoiding sweet things and brushing well after every meal, and seeing a dental worker right away, since if seen soon enough the tooth can often be cleaned and filled so it will last for many years. The chapter warns not to wait until a tooth with a cavity hurts a lot before having it filled.
when_to_seek_care: See a dental worker right away if a tooth has a cavity; do not wait until it hurts a lot.

symptom: toothache with swelling, pus or large tender lymph nodes (tooth abscess)
citation: Chapter 17: The Teeth, Gums, and Mouth
summary: A toothache results when a cavity becomes infected, and an abscess results when the infection reaches the tip of a root and forms a pocket of pus. To calm the pain the book advises cleaning the hole in the tooth, removing all food particles, rinsing the mouth with warm salt water, and taking a pain medicine. If the tooth infection is severe, shown by swelling, pus or large tender lymph nodes, the book points to an antibiotic on its medicine pages. Abscesses should be treated right away, before the infection spreads to other parts of the body.
danger_signs: swelling
pus
large tender lymph nodes
when_to_seek_care: Treat abscesses right away; if pain and swelling do not go away or keep coming back, the tooth should probably be pulled, which requires a dental or health worker.

alternate_names: muscle pain with fever and eye swelling
citation: Chapter 12: Trichinosis
danger_signs: fever with chills, muscle pain, swelling around the eyes and sometimes feet, small bruises on the skin, bleeding in the whites of the eyes
severe cases lasting 3 or 4 weeks
summary: Trichinosis worms burrow through the intestines into the muscles and are never seen in stools. People get them, like tapeworms, from eating infected pork or other meat that is not well cooked. From a few hours to five days after eating infected pork, the person may develop diarrhea and feel sick to the stomach. In serious cases there may be fever with chills, muscle pain, swelling around the eyes and sometimes feet, small bruises on the skin, and bleeding in the whites of the eyes.
symptom: trichinosis
when_to_seek_care: Seek medical help at once; if several people who ate meat from the same pig get sick afterward, suspect trichinosis and seek medical attention.

symptom: trouble seeing clearly, headaches or eye pain when reading, or difficulty seeing close things with age
citation: Chapter 16: The Eyes
summary: Children who have trouble seeing clearly or who get headaches or eye pain when they read may need glasses and should have their eyes examined. In older people it is common that with passing years it becomes more difficult to see close things clearly, and reading glasses often help, chosen to let the person see clearly about forty centimetres away. If glasses do not help, the book advises seeing an eye doctor. Chapter 22 repeats this for people after forty, noting that many become farsighted and that glasses will often help, and adds that every child's eyesight should be checked as early as possible, best around four years.
danger_signs: loss of vision in one or both eyes
when_to_seek_care: See an eye doctor if glasses do not help, and if sight is poor in one or both eyes.

citation: Chapter 5: Healing Without Medicines; Chapter 4: How to Take Care of a Sick Person
danger_signs: twelve hours or more without being able to urinate
blood in the urine
summary: Minor urinary infections, described as common in women, are presented in Chapter 5 as a case where drinking plenty of water may help more than medicines. Chapter 4 gives the opposite warning for severe cases, listing twelve hours or more without being able to urinate among signs of dangerous illness, and noting that a very sick adult should urinate a reasonable amount several times daily, with low urine output prompting encouragement to drink more and watch for dehydration. Blood in the urine is also listed in Chapter 4 among signs of dangerous illness. This entry keeps the mild water-care point separate from the danger thresholds, which must not be confused.
symptom: trouble urinating and minor urinary infection
when_to_seek_care: Seek medical help as soon as possible for twelve hours or more without being able to urinate, or for blood in the urine.

citation: Chapter 14: Tuberculosis (TB)
danger_signs: coughing up blood
pale waxy skin
voice growing hoarse, which is very serious
in children: steady weight loss, frequent fever, less energy for play, swellings in neck or belly
summary: Tuberculosis of the lungs is a chronic contagious disease that often strikes people aged fifteen to thirty-five, especially those weak, poorly nourished, living in crowded conditions, with HIV, or living with someone who has TB. Most frequent signs are a cough lasting longer than three weeks, often worse just after waking, slight fever in the evening and sweating at night, pain in the chest or upper back, and chronic loss of appetite and weight with increasing weakness. In young children the cough may come late, so weight loss, frequent fever and less energy are watched for.
symptom: tuberculosis
when_to_seek_care: Seek medical help at the first sign of tuberculosis, at a health center where sputum can be tested.

citation: Chapter 14: Typhoid Fever
danger_signs: shitting blood
signs of peritonitis or pneumonia
delirium, weakness, weight loss and dehydration in the second week
summary: Typhoid is an infection of the gut affecting the whole body, spread feces-to-mouth in contaminated food and water and often coming in epidemics. In the first week it begins like a cold or flu, with headache, sore throat and often a dry cough, vomiting, diarrhea or constipation, and fever that goes up and down but rises a little more each day to forty degrees or more, with a pulse often relatively slow for the fever. In the second week there is high fever with slow pulse, a few pink spots, trembling, delirium, weakness, weight loss and dehydration.
symptom: typhoid fever
when_to_seek_care: Seek medical help; if the person shits blood or develops signs of peritonitis or pneumonia, take her to a hospital at once.

citation: Chapter 14: Typhus
danger_signs: fever lasting 2 weeks or more
epidemic typhus especially dangerous
large painful sore at a tick bite with swollen painful lymph nodes nearby
summary: Typhus is similar to but different from typhoid, transmitted by bites of lice, ticks or rat fleas. It begins like a bad cold, then after a week or more fever begins with chills, headache and pain in the muscles and chest. After a few days of fever a typical rash appears, first in the armpits then on the body, arms and legs but not on the face, palms or soles, looking like many tiny bruises. The fever lasts two weeks or more, is usually mild in children and very severe in old people. In tick-spread typhus there is often a large painful sore at the bite.
symptom: typhus
when_to_seek_care: If someone may have typhus, get medical advice, as special tests are often needed.

symptom: vaginal discharge that is grey, yellow or green and smells bad, with pain during sex or burning when urinating (trichomonas infection)
citation: Chapter 18: The Urinary System and the Genitals
summary: It is normal to have vaginal discharge that is clear, white or thick, varying in amount at different times in the menstrual cycle, when using hormonal contraception, or during pregnancy, and if there is no itching or bad smell there is probably no problem. When discharge is an unusual colour, has a bad smell, or comes with itching or pain in or around the vagina, belly pain, pain while urinating or having sex, or fever, it may be caused by an infection, some of which are dangerous if not treated quickly. Discharge that is grey, yellow or green and smells bad is probably an infection of Trichomonas, with possible pain during sex or burning when urinating. The book advises antibiotic treatment as directed on its medicine pages, treating the partner at the same time, and soothing sitz baths.
when_to_seek_care: If any discharge lasts a long time or does not get better with treatment, see a health worker.

symptom: vaginal discharge with blood in it, or with fever or pain in the lower belly
citation: Chapter 18: The Urinary System and the Genitals
summary: Discharge with blood in it, or that comes with fever or pain in the lower belly, may be a sign of a more serious infection according to the chapter's vaginal discharge section. This is presented as a distinct warning presentation rather than as one of the three named discharge infections, and the book gives no separate cause or treatment for it in this section. It sits alongside the general advice that unusual discharge with itching, pain, belly pain, pain while urinating or having sex, or fever may be caused by an infection, some of which are dangerous if not treated quickly.
danger_signs: blood in vaginal discharge
fever
pain in the lower belly
when_to_seek_care: Get medical help right away.

symptom: vaginal irritation from spermicide used frequently, or from herbs, plants or harsh chemicals put in the vagina to make it dry
citation: Chapter 20: Family Planning
summary: Spermicide does not work well by itself but gives extra protection when used with a condom or diaphragm, and it does not protect against sexually transmitted infections or HIV. If used frequently, spermicide can irritate the vagina, making it easier for the woman to get an infection including HIV. Separately, the chapter warns that putting herbs, plants or harsh chemicals in the vagina to make it dry only causes irritation of the skin inside the vagina, making it easier for women to get infections, and that such substances do not prevent pregnancy. Douching after sex also does not prevent pregnancy and can push sperm up into the womb.
when_to_seek_care: not stated in the book

citation: Chapter 13: Varicose Veins
summary: Varicose veins are veins that are swollen, twisted and often painful, often seen on the legs of older people and of women who are pregnant or have had many children. There is no medicine for them, but the book advises not spending much time standing or sitting with feet down, lying down with feet up above the level of the heart for a few minutes every half hour if standing or sitting is unavoidable, walking in place or lifting heels when standing, sleeping with feet up, and using elastic stockings or bandages, removed at night.
symptom: varicose veins
when_to_seek_care: not stated in the book

symptom: very itchy rash, welts or hives that come and go rapidly (allergic skin reaction)
citation: Chapter 15: Skin Problems
summary: Touching, eating, injecting or breathing certain things can cause an itching rash or hives in allergic people. Hives are thick, raised spots or patches that look like bee stings and itch greatly, and may come and go rapidly or move from one spot to another. The book warns to watch for reactions caused by certain medicines, especially penicillin injections and antivenoms made from horse serum, with a rash or hives appearing from minutes to ten days after injection. If an itching rash or hives follow a medicine, the book says to stop using it and never use that medicine again.
danger_signs: allergic shock (the book cross-refers to its allergic shock section)
when_to_seek_care: The book points to its allergic reactions section for more detail; no separate care threshold is stated in this chapter beyond stopping the causative medicine.

symptom: very itchy small bumps, especially between fingers, wrists, waist, genitals and toes (scabies)
citation: Chapter 15: Skin Problems
summary: The book describes scabies as very itchy little bumps that can appear all over the body but are most common between the fingers, on the wrists, around the waist, on the genitals and between the toes, and usually not on the head and face except in babies. It is caused by tiny animals tunnelling under the skin and spreads by touch or through clothes and bedding. Scratching can cause infected sores with pus, swollen lymph nodes or fever. Signs may take weeks to appear on a first infection and days on a later one, and itching may last up to two weeks after treatment.
danger_signs: sores with pus
swollen lymph nodes
fever
when_to_seek_care: Seek medical help if a serious skin problem gets worse in spite of treatment; the book does not give a separate care threshold for scabies itself, so for persistent signs after two weeks it advises repeating treatment or trying a different one.

symptom: very sick child lying with head tilted way back, neck too stiff to bend forward, and body making strange movements (meningitis in a child)
citation: Chapter 21: Health and Sicknesses of Children
summary: Meningitis is described as a dangerous disease that may come as a complication of measles, mumps or another serious illness, and children of mothers who have tuberculosis may get tubercular meningitis. A very sick child who lies with the head tilted way back, whose neck is too stiff to bend forward, and whose body makes strange movements such as seizures may have meningitis. Chapter 19 adds newborn clues: a swollen soft spot on top of the head may mean meningitis, and if the baby is too stiff to put the head between the knees or cries out in pain, it is probably meningitis. No treatment is given in Chapter 21 itself beyond cross-referring to the meningitis section.
danger_signs: head tilted way back
neck too stiff to bend forward
strange movements or seizures
swollen soft spot on a baby's head
when_to_seek_care: not stated in the book

citation: Chapter 4: How to Take Care of a Sick Person; Chapter 9: Instructions and Precautions for Injections; Chapter 13: Vomiting
danger_signs: constant gut pain, especially if the person cannot defecate or no gurgles are heard in the belly
dehydration that increases and cannot be controlled
heavy vomiting lasting more than one day, or more than a few hours in babies
severe vomiting lasting more than 24 hours
strong, continuous stomach pains with vomiting in a person who does not have diarrhea or cannot have a bowel movement
violent vomiting, especially dark green, brown, or smelling like feces
vomit with blood or feces
vomiting of blood
summary: Vomiting appears as part of several presentations, including diarrhea with vomiting in a dehydrated baby, food poisoning with sudden vomiting followed by diarrhea, cramps, and weakness, and a severe allergic reaction with vomiting and diarrhea. Chapter 4 lists heavy vomiting lasting more than one day, or more than a few hours in babies, among signs of dangerous illness. Chapter 9 lists vomiting that cannot be controlled as a case where injection may be needed when help is delayed, and lists vomiting often, inability to swallow, or unconsciousness as situations where injection rather than medicine by mouth may be appropriate. A very sick person who can barely swallow should be given small sips often.
symptom: vomiting
when_to_seek_care: Seek medical help as soon as possible for heavy vomiting lasting more than one day, or more than a few hours in babies; get help as fast as you can if vomiting cannot be controlled.

symptom: warm, painful swelling under the skin that may break open and drain pus (boil or abscess)
citation: Chapter 15: Skin Problems
summary: A boil or abscess is an infection forming a sac of pus under the skin, which can happen when a hair root is infected or from a puncture wound or an injection given with a dirty needle. It is painful and the skin around it becomes red and hot, and it can cause swollen lymph nodes and fever. The book advises hot compresses several times a day, letting the boil break open by itself, never pressing or squeezing it, and continuing hot compresses after it opens to allow pus to drain.
danger_signs: swollen lymph nodes
fever
when_to_seek_care: Get medical help if the abscess is very painful and does not open after two or three days of hot soaks, so it can be cut open for drainage if needed.

symptom: warning signs while using combined birth control pills: severe headaches with blurred vision, weakness or numbness in arms or legs, severe chest pain and shortness of breath, severe pain in one leg, or severe abdominal pain
citation: Chapter 20: Family Planning
summary: The chapter gives a warning-sign list for problems with combined pills, presented here exactly as a presentation to act on rather than as a diagnosis. A person using combined pills should stop taking the pill and see a health worker if they have severe headaches with blurred vision that begin after starting the pill, feel weakness or numbness in the arms or legs, feel severe pain in the chest and shortness of breath, have severe pain in one leg, or have severe pain in the abdomen. The chapter adds that if any of these problems occur, pregnancy can also be dangerous, so another type of family planning such as condoms should be used until the person can see a health worker trained in hormonal family planning methods.
danger_signs: severe headaches with blurred vision beginning after starting the pill
weakness or numbness in arms or legs
severe chest pain and shortness of breath
severe pain in one leg
severe abdominal pain
when_to_seek_care: Stop taking the pill and see a health worker; use another method such as condoms until seen by a health worker trained in hormonal family planning methods.

symptom: warts, including painful wart-like spots on the sole of the foot and wart-like growths on the genitals
citation: Chapter 15: Skin Problems
summary: Most warts, especially those in children, last three to five years and go away by themselves. Flat, painful wart-like spots on the sole of the foot are often plantar warts, though they may be corns. The book warns that it is safer not to use strong acids or poisonous plants on warts, as these may cause burns or sores much worse than the warts, and that painful plantar warts can sometimes be removed by a health worker. For warts on the penis, vagina or around the anus the book cross-refers to its genital warts section rather than giving treatment here.
when_to_seek_care: not stated in the book

citation: Chapter 11: Severe Malnutrition, Dry Malnutrition or Marasmus
summary: Dry malnutrition, or marasmus, happens when a child does not get enough of any kind of food and is effectively starved. The child's body is small, very thin and wasted, little more than skin and bones. The book says this child needs more food, especially energy foods, and notes that severe malnutrition often starts when a child has diarrhea or another infection, and is most common in babies who stopped breastfeeding early or suddenly without sufficient high energy foods often enough.
symptom: wasting in a child
when_to_seek_care: not stated in the book

symptom: weakness and tiredness in an older person, worsened by poor eating
citation: Chapter 22: Health and Sicknesses of Older People
summary: Old people understandably have less energy and strength than when younger, but they will become even weaker if they do not eat well. Although older people often do not eat very much, the book advises that they should eat some body-building and protective foods every day, cross-referring to its nutrition chapter. This is a general presentation rather than a specific disease, and no danger signs or referral threshold are stated for weakness and tiredness alone in this chapter, distinct from the weakness, dizziness and tiredness listed as part of heart trouble, which is indexed separately.
when_to_seek_care: not stated in the book

citation: Chapter 3: How to Examine a Sick Person
danger_signs: the person is so weak they faint when they stand up
sudden weakness or drooping on one side of the face or body
summary: Weakness, numbness, and loss of control are presented as complaints to test by comparing both sides of the body, watching how the person walks and moves, and comparing hand strength and leg movement. Sudden facial drooping or weakness may suggest head injury, stroke, or Bell's palsy, while slow onset may suggest a brain tumour and needs medical advice. Uneven muscle loss or weakness in children suggests polio first, and in adults a back problem, back or head injury, or stroke. Loss of feeling in or near spots or patches is linked with leprosy, loss in both hands or feet with diabetes or leprosy, and loss on one side with a back problem or injury.
symptom: weakness, numbness or loss of feeling
when_to_seek_care: Seek medical help as soon as possible if the person is so weak they faint when standing up; get medical advice for slow-onset weakness that may suggest a brain tumour.

citation: Chapter 12: Whipworm (Trichuris)
danger_signs: part of the intestines coming out of the anus in children
summary: Whipworms are pink or gray worms three to five centimeters long, passed feces-to-mouth like roundworms. Usually this worm does little harm, but it may cause diarrhea, and in children it occasionally causes part of the intestines to come out of the anus. Prevention is the same as for roundworm: latrines, handwashing before eating or handling food, protecting food from flies, and following the chapter's cleanliness guidelines.
symptom: whipworm infection
when_to_seek_care: not stated in the book

symptom: white, lumpy vaginal discharge like milk curd or yogurt, with severe itching, red painful genitals, and pain while urinating or having sex (yeast infection)
citation: Chapter 18: The Urinary System and the Genitals
summary: White, lumpy discharge from the vagina that looks like milk curd or yogurt could be a yeast infection, with itching that may be severe, genitals that often hurt and look red, and pain while urinating or having sex. This infection is especially common during pregnancy and in people who have diabetes, HIV, or have been taking antibiotics. The book advises vaginal inserts or cream for Candida as directed on its medicine pages, mentions unsweetened yogurt in the vagina as a home remedy said to help control yeast infections, and warns never to use antibiotics for a yeast infection because they can make it worse.
when_to_seek_care: If any discharge lasts a long time or does not get better with treatment, see a health worker.

symptom: white patches or spots in the mouth, including a white-coated tongue, tiny white spots like salt grains in a child with fever, and small white patches like milk curds stuck to raw meat (thrush)
citation: Chapter 17: The Teeth, Gums, and Mouth
summary: Many illnesses cause a white or yellowish coating on the tongue and roof of the mouth, which is common when there is a fever and is not serious, though rinsing with warm water, salt and bicarbonate of soda several times a day helps. Tiny white spots like salt grains in the mouth of a child with fever may be an early sign of measles. Thrush is different: small white patches on the inside of the mouth and tongue that look like milk curds stuck to raw meat, caused by a yeast infection. Thrush is common in newborn babies, in people with HIV, and in people using certain antibiotics. The book advises stopping the antibiotic unless it is very important to keep taking it, and using an antifungal treatment as directed on its medicine pages, with yogurt said to possibly help.
danger_signs: thrush moving into the throat and making it hard to swallow
when_to_seek_care: In very severe cases, or if thrush moves into the throat and makes it hard to swallow, consult a health worker, as a stronger medicine may be needed.
review_note: Grouped three white-mouth presentations that the chapter presents together but that have different meanings (harmless fever coating, possible early measles, thrush); a reader should not use this entry alone to tell them apart.

symptom: whooping cough in a child: cold-like start with fever, runny nose and cough, then rapid coughing many times without breath until sticky mucus is coughed up and air rushes back with a loud whoop, lips and nails turning blue, vomiting after coughing
citation: Chapter 21: Health and Sicknesses of Children
summary: Whooping cough begins a week or two after being exposed to a child who has it, starting like a cold with fever, a runny nose and cough. Two weeks later the whoop begins: the child coughs rapidly many times without taking a breath until coughing up a plug of sticky mucus, and air rushes back into the lungs with a loud whoop. While coughing the lips and nails may turn blue for lack of air, and after the whoop the child may vomit. Between coughing spells the child seems fairly healthy, and whooping cough often lasts three months or more. It is especially dangerous in babies under one year, and small babies do not develop the typical whoop, so fits of coughing with swollen or puffy eyes when cases are in the area should be treated as whooping cough at once.
danger_signs: lips and nails turning blue
baby stopping breathing after a cough
seizures
signs of pneumonia
bright red bleeding inside the white of the eyes from coughing
when_to_seek_care: If seizures or signs of pneumonia develop, get medical help; if the baby stops breathing after a cough, turn the baby over, pull sticky mucus from the mouth with a finger, and slap the back with the flat of the hand.

citation: Chapter 1: Home Cures and Popular Beliefs; Chapter 5: Healing Without Medicines
danger_signs: loss of large amounts of blood from anywhere in the body
sores that keep growing and do not go away with treatment
summary: Wounds are discussed in terms of cleaning and stopping bleeding without harmful remedies. Cardon cactus juice is described as usable to clean wounds when there is no boiled water, and as helping stop a wound from bleeding because it makes cut blood vessels squeeze shut, after which the wound should later be cleaned with boiled water and soap. Chapter 5 stresses washing wounds well with soap and clean water to help prevent infection and tetanus, and using hot soaks or compresses for infected wounds, abscesses, and boils. Chapter 4 adds that soiled or bloodstained items from a person with infectious disease should be washed in hot soapy water.
symptom: wounds and bleeding
when_to_seek_care: Seek medical help as soon as possible for loss of large amounts of blood from anywhere in the body.

alternate_names: sudden fever with chills and body aches
fever returning with jaundice and bleeding
citation: Chapter 14: Dengue, Zika, Chikungunya, and Yellow Fever, Yellow Fever
danger_signs: fever returning later with jaundice, belly pain, vomiting, or bleeding from mouth, nose or eyes
summary: Yellow fever is spread by mosquitoes and starts suddenly with fever, chills, body aches, headache, nausea sometimes with vomiting, and weakness, with no rash. The illness usually goes away after three or four days. If fever returns later with jaundice, belly pain, vomiting, or bleeding from the mouth, nose or eyes, this severe form needs hospital care right away. A vaccine prevents the illness, and care is rest, liquids and acetaminophen for pain and fever, not aspirin or ibuprofen.
symptom: yellow fever
when_to_seek_care: The severe form with returning fever, jaundice, belly pain, vomiting or bleeding needs hospital care right away.

citation: Chapter 3: How to Examine a Sick Person; Chapter 2: Sicknesses that Are Often Confused
summary: Yellow colour of the skin and eyes, called jaundice, is presented as a sign that may result from disease in the liver, including hepatitis, cirrhosis, or amebic abscess, or from gallbladder disease, and it may also occur in newborn babies and in children born with sickle cell disease. In the fever discussion, hepatitis is sketched as loss of appetite, nausea, eyes and skin turning yellow, orange or brown urine, whitish stools, sometimes a large tender liver, mild fever, and great weakness. Chapter 3 advises noting eye colour, whether white, red, or yellow, as part of examining a sick person. This entry does not distinguish the many liver and blood causes.
symptom: yellow skin and eyes
when_to_seek_care: not stated in the book

alternate_names: fever with rash and irritated eyes
citation: Chapter 14: Dengue, Zika, Chikungunya, and Yellow Fever, Zika
danger_signs: harm to a baby growing in the womb
review_note: Zika often has no signs, so this entry is based on the signs the book does list plus its pregnancy warning; a reviewer should check whether a no-signs presentation needs a separate handling note.
summary: Zika can cause fever, rash, body aches and irritated eyes, or have no signs at all. Most people get it from mosquitoes, but it can also pass during sex. Zika can harm a baby growing in the womb, so if pregnant, the book advises avoiding mosquito bites and using condoms during sex. As with the other mosquito illnesses in this section, no medicine cures it, and care is rest, liquids and acetaminophen for pain and fever, not aspirin or ibuprofen.
symptom: zika
when_to_seek_care: not stated in the book
